findings.issue_text: [BUG] `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` (containing a raw `datetime` in the `queued` field) as Celery task kwargs; with the default JSON serializer this raises `EncodeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable`, so the assignee-sync task never enqueues and inbound integration assignee propagation silently breaks on real deployments.

[BUG] `AssignmentSource.queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default evaluated once at module import; since the class is frozen and `from_integration` never sets it, every instance carries the process-start timestamp instead of the actual queue time, making `to_dict()["queued"]` wrong for freshness/ordering consumers.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` silently returns `None` on any schema mismatch and the task treats `None` as "no source", re-enabling the exact sync-loop the diff was meant to prevent during rolling deploys or dict-shape drift, with no error surfaced to operators.

[ADVISORY] The round-trip through the actual Celery transport is never tested: `test_to_dict` only checks dict contents and other tests run under `self.tasks()` with in-process pickle execution, so the JSON-serializer failure has zero coverage in the production serializer configuration.

[ADVISORY] The loop guard `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` depends on every integration correctly overriding `should_sync` with the new two-arg signature; `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` ignores `sync_source`, so subclasses that don't forward it silently lose loop protection, and the guard lives in an overridable hook rather than enforced at the `sync_group_assignee_outbound` call site.

[BUG] `sync_assignee_outbound` task passes `assignment_source` kwarg but the abstract signature and all provider implementations (Jira, VSTS, etc.) were never updated to accept it, causing `TypeError` that kills the celery task and breaks outbound assignee sync entirely

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default evaluated once at module import, so every `AssignmentSource.from_integration(...)` instance carries the server-process start time instead of the enqueue time; any dedup/latency logic keyed on `queued` reports process uptime instead of sync delay, and the test only asserts `queued is not None` so it cannot catch this

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` returns a `datetime` in the dict passed to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`, causing `EncodeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` with the standard JSON serializer, so any assignment with a source never enqueues its outbound task, silently disabling cross-system propagation on the inbound path

[ADVISORY] `sync_status_outbound` / `sync_status_inbound` got a new `assignment_source` parameter in the abstract signature but no caller anywhere passes one, making it dead surface with no implementation or test coverage; a resolve-triggered status ping-pong between two linked systems is not prevented, which is the sync-cycle class of bug this PR claims to fix

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` returns `None` on any parse failure and the task treats `None` as 'no source', which passes `should_sync` unconditionally, so a malformed/partially-serialized payload silently disables cycle prevention and re-opens the infinite sync loop; the failure should be loud (log + drop the sync) rather than a silent fallback

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` performs no type validation, so a string `integration_id` (e.g., from JSON) constructs a 'valid' `AssignmentSource` where the same-integration cycle check compares str to int, evaluates `False`, and bypasses cycle prevention

[ADVISORY] The task's new parsing/dispatch logic (`from_dict` → `should_sync` → `sync_assignee_outbound` with parsed `assignment_source`) has no test executing the positive case where a non-matching source flows through the task; the only task-path test asserts the negative (not-called) branch, so round-trip regressions ship undetected

[ADVISORY] Tests assert only the `None` return of `from_dict`; no test covers the JSON-round-trip shape the task actually produces (`to_dict` → broker → `from_dict`), including whether `queued` survives as a datetime or string, leaving the serialization contract between producer and consumer unverified

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default evaluated once at module import, so every `AssignmentSource` carries the same frozen import-time timestamp instead of the actual enqueue time, silently breaking any logic or observability keyed on `queued`.

[BUG] `to_dict` returns `asdict(self)` keeping `queued` as a raw `datetime`, which is passed directly as a Celery task kwarg; with the default JSON serializer this raises `TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable`, so the outbound task never enqueues and assigning a Sentry issue from an external system errors on the assign path.

[ADVISORY] `sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter but no call site passes it and no implementer uses it, creating dead signature churn and falsely implying status cycle-prevention that `should_sync` cannot deliver.

[ADVISORY] Under-scoping: `AssignmentSource` is threaded only through the assignee path, so `sync_status_inbound` and status-outbound never attach a source, allowing status sync loops (A↔A or A↔B) despite the PR claiming cross-system cycle prevention.
[ADVISORY] `source_name` is written by `from_integration` and round-tripped through serialization but read by nothing; `should_sync` compares only `integration_id`, making the field redundant.

[ADVISORY] `AssignmentSource.from_dict` swallows malformed payloads to `None` with no logging, silently re-enabling outbound sync to the originating integration (the exact cycle this diff prevents) — the safety check fails open instead of closed.

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` default is evaluated once at class-definition/import time, so every AssignmentSource constructed without explicit `queued` shares the same frozen timestamp (import time), making the field semantically dead for stale/replay detection; the `test_to_dict` assertion passes while the value is wrong

[BUG] `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` embeds a raw `datetime` in Celery task kwargs, causing `EncodeError` with a JSON-serializing broker so every outbound assignee sync from an inbound integration assignment fails to enqueue; on the pickle path `from_dict` reconstructs `queued` as a string due to unenforced annotations, causing round-trip format drift

[BUG] `from_dict` returns `None` on `TypeError` from any schema mismatch (unknown keys, missing fields, newer producer payloads), silently degrading to 'no assignment source' so `should_sync` skips the cycle check and re-enables the integration sync loop; rejecting should fail-safe (skip outbound) not fail-unsafe (sync as if no source existed)

[ADVISORY] Cycle-prevention design covers only assignee sync: no caller passes `assignment_source` to `sync_status_outbound` and the inbound status path never constructs or propagates an AssignmentSource, so cross-system status sync cycles (resolve→unresolve ping-pong) remain possible despite the PR implying broad cross-system synchronization

[ADVISORY] `groupassignee.py` (core region-silo model) imports `sentry.integrations.services.assignment_source` at module level, inverting the dependency direction (models → integration service layer); any future integration dependency in AssignmentSource would break silo layering — it belongs in a shared kernel/neutral module

[ADVISORY] `test_from_dict_empty_array` tests an empty dict not an array, and the test suite never exercises `to_dict → from_dict` round-tripping — the exact production path through Celery kwargs — so the queued field format drift and datetime serialization failure are invisible to CI

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` puts a raw `datetime` (`queued` field, from `asdict()`) into Celery task kwargs via `apply_async`; with the default JSON task serializer this raises `EncodeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable`, so every outbound assignee sync from an inbound integration assignment fails to enqueue and cross-integration propagation silently never happens (only works if broker uses pickle, which Sentry's celery defaults do not).

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition (module import) time, not per instance, so every `AssignmentSource` reports the server's process-start time as `queued` — fabricated data that breaks staleness/ordering decisions. Should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

[ADVISORY] `sync_status_outbound` gained an `assignment_source` parameter but no caller in the diff passes it, and `sync_status_inbound` never constructs or propagates an `AssignmentSource` — status-resolution sync loops remain fully possible, indicating intent drift; either the parameter is dead and should be deleted or status cycle prevention was cut without an explicit decision.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` swallows all `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None`, which the caller in `sync_assignee_outbound.py:53` treats identically to "no source" — a malformed dict silently disables cycle prevention and reopens the sync loop with no log line or analytics event.

[ADVISORY] The new cycle-prevention behavior is gated only by `organizations:integrations-issue-sync` with no new feature flag or release note; existing single-integration customers with inbound and outbound assignee sync lose the confirmatory echo write and the `integration.issue.assignee.synced` analytics event, with no way to disable the change short of a code revert.

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` at assignment_source.py:19 is evaluated once at class-definition (import) time, so every AssignmentSource instance and serialized task payload carries the process-start timestamp, not the actual queue time; the field is unfixable without a default_factory.

[BUG] `to_dict()` emits a raw datetime into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`, and celery's default JSON serializer cannot encode datetime, causing an EncodeError on every inbound-triggered assignee change; outbound assignee sync is silently broken whenever assignment_source is non-None, and the new tests only cover assignment_source=None and should_sync=False paths.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` swallows all malformed payloads by returning None, and None is treated as 'no source provided' (cycle prevention disabled) rather than a hard failure, so corrupt payloads silently re-enable the sync loop and cause duplicate/bouncing assignments with no operator signal.

[ADVISORY] `sync_group_assignee_outbound.apply_async` now always passes a fourth kwarg `assignment_source_dict`; during a rolling deploy, old workers running the pre-diff task signature raise TypeError: unexpected keyword argument, breaking assignee outbound sync for the deploy window; no versioning/backward-compat handling on the task signature.

[ADVISORY] test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration only covers the block half of cycle prevention; no test constructs a source from integration A and asserts sync still fires through integration B, so an over-blocking regression (e.g., if sync_source: returning False for any non-None source) passes the suite and legitimate cross-integration sync silently dies

[ADVISORY] The deassign cycle-prevention branch in groupassignee.py:235-239 (passing assignment_source into sync_group_assignee_outbound on unassign) has zero test coverage: no test calls deassign(..., assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)) and asserts sync_assignee_outbound is not called, so a regression in the deassign-side source plumbing is invisible

[BUG] The to_dict/from_dict round-trip actually performed in production (sync.py:137-142 sends via Celery apply_async, sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-55 reconstructs) is never tested; test_from_dict_valid_data only passes {"source_name", "integration_id"} and never does from_dict(source.to_dict()), which would expose that queued arrives as a string (or fails to serialize) after JSON serialization through the broker and from_dict happily accepts it

[ADVISORY] test_from_dict_empty_array tests an empty dict but is named "array", and no test covers the sentinel-semantics hazard of a dict with correct keys but wrong types (e.g., integration_id: "123") being accepted and returning a live AssignmentSource with a string id, causing the integration_id == comparison in should_sync to silently compare int to str and disable cycle prevention for payloads that lost type fidelity in transit

[ADVISED] test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign duplicates the post-assign assertions (GroupAssignee row + Activity) from the pre-existing test body into the new matching-source test, so the shared assertion block lives in two hand-maintained copies; drift between them will mask which behavior is actually under test (deletion opportunity: extract or leave the assertions only in the base test)

[BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` in `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:17` is evaluated once at class-definition (import) time, so every `AssignmentSource` built via `from_integration` gets a stale shared timestamp that cannot represent when the assignment actually happened.

[BUG] `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)` including a raw `datetime` for `queued` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:137-143, assignment_source.py:30), which is not JSON-serializable, so `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` raises `TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` and the outbound assignee sync is never enqueued.

[ADVISORY] Rolling-deploy skew: new-code web workers enqueue `sync_assignee_outbound` tasks carrying `assignment_source_dict` while old-code task workers don't accept the kwarg, raising `TypeError` and losing assignee syncs enqueued during the deploy window; passing the field only when non-None would shrink the window.

[ADVISORY] `from_dict` (assignment_source.py:31-35) swallows malformed payloads by returning `None`, which disables the cycle-prevention check in `should_sync` — e.g., a string `queued` from JSON round-trip is not datetime-parsed, silently recreating the sync loop this PR exists to prevent; tests don't cover the string-datetime shape.

[ADVISORY] The `sync_status_outbound` signature gained an `assignment_source` parameter (issues.py:411-418) but no caller passes it and no implementation reads it — concrete overrides that don't accept the kwarg will raise `TypeError` when it's eventually forwarded, and the status-sync loop remains unbroken.

[ADVISORY] Coverage gap: no test that `deassign(group, assignment_source=...)` actually suppresses the outbound unassign for the originating integration (groupassignee.py:189-192); a regression in the `deassign` branch (groupassignee.py:237-239) would reintroduce un-assign loops with no failing test.

[BUG] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:15 — queued: datetime = timezone.now() is a class-definition-time default: every AssignmentSource created via from_integration gets the timestamp of module import, not the actual queueing time; the field is structurally guaranteed to never hold the real queue time, so any latency/staleness logic keyed on queued computes against a frozen import-time constant.

[BUG] sync.py:134-141 + assignment_source.py:20 — assignment_source.to_dict() is put into apply_async(kwargs=...) containing a raw datetime (queued); Celery's default JSON encoder cannot serialize datetime, so the enqueue raises TypeError at dispatch time and the assignee sync to the external issue never runs; even with a custom serializer, the JSON round-trip turns queued into a string that from_dict (cls(**input_dict)) accepts without validation, leaving a str where the type declares datetime.

[BUG] sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-56 — AssignmentSource.from_dict returns None on any malformed dict, and None is treated identically to 'no source', so cycle suppression is silently disabled; a dict that fails to reconstruct causes should_sync('outbound_assignee', None) to return True and the same integration syncs the assignment back out — the exact sync loop this diff was built to prevent — with no log, no error, and analytics recording a successful 'synced' that is actually an echo.

[ADVISORY] sync_assignee_outbound.py:27-33 — rolling-deploy skew: the task gains a new required-by-signature kwarg assignment_source_dict and the producer at sync.py:134 sends it unconditionally with no feature flag or options gate; during a rolling deploy, old workers running the old signature raise TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict' and every queued assignee sync for the deploy window fails, leaving external issues out of sync with no user-visible error.

[ADVISORY] issues.py:382-389 — the same-integration suppression only checks sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id with no timestamp/expiry enforced despite the dataclass carrying queued; a queued inbound sync that lands long after a user manually re-assigns in Sentry is suppressed if the stale assignment originates from that integration, so the desync window is unbounded and queued is dead weight needing either an expiry check or deletion.

[ADVISORY] issues.py:16 — sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter (issues.py:411-419) and should_sync now accepts it, but sync_status_inbound and the status-sync path never populate sync_source, so status echoes (the other half of the sync loop) remain unprotected: a resolve in Jira round-trips back to the same Jira issue; the stated goal of preventing sync-cycles is only enforced for the assignee attribute.

[ADVISORY] tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:200-219 — the new suppression test asserts only mock_sync_assignee_outbound.assert_not_called() for the matching-integration case; there is no test that a different integration's AssignmentSource still syncs, nor that a user-originated assign with no source syncs through the new kwargs path end-to-end, so a regression that over-broadens the should_sync suppression (e.g. suppressing whenever sync_source is truthy) passes the entire suite while cross-system propagation silently stops.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` returning `None` on any missing/extra/invalid fields (catches `ValueError`/`TypeError`) with no logging, and `sync_assignee_outbound()` then passes that `None` into `installation.should_sync(...)`. Since `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync()` only blocks cycles when `sync_source` is non-`None` and matches `self.org_integration.integration_id`, a parse failure effectively disables the new loop-prevention for that task run. However, the diff does not demonstrate that such malformed `assignment_source_dict` will occur in normal operation (the producer uses `assignment_source.to_dict()`), so this is a robustness/operability concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` returning `asdict(self)`, which includes `queued: datetime` (see `assignment_source.py`). That dict is passed into Celery via `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (`integrations/utils/sync.py`). Existing tests only assert dict contents (`test_to_dict`) and invoke tasks under `self.tasks()` (eager/in-process execution), but do not exercise serialization of `assignment_source_dict` through the configured Celery serializer. Given the new payload contains a `datetime`, this is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in coverage around whether Celery transport/serializer will accept it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loop guard `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` depends on every integration correctly overriding `should_sync` with the new two-arg signature; `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` ignores `sync_source`, so subclasses that don't forward it silently lose loop protection, and the guard lives in an overridable hook rather than enforced at the `sync_group_assignee_outbound` call site.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds loop-cycle protection only inside `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` (issues.py) by returning `False` when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`. That protection is not enforced at the `sync_group_assignee_outbound` call site (utils/sync.py) and lives in an overridable hook (`should_sync`). If a concrete integration overrides `should_sync` (or bypasses it) and does not apply/forward the `sync_source` check, the cycle guard would not apply. The claim that it “depends on every integration correctly overriding the new two-arg signature” is somewhat speculative from this diff alone (we can’t see other subclasses), but the architectural risk that the guard is optional/overridable is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `sync_assignee_outbound` task passes `assignment_source` kwarg but the abstract signature and all provider implementations (Jira, VSTS, etc.) were never updated to accept it, causing `TypeError` that kills the celery task and breaks outbound assignee sync entirely

adjudication.rationale: The diff updates the `sync_assignee_outbound` Celery task to call `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py), but the integration base/mixin changes only update `should_sync` and `sync_status_outbound` to accept an `AssignmentSource`; there is no corresponding update shown for the abstract/provider-facing `sync_assignee_outbound` method signature in mixins/issues.py. If existing integration installations implement `sync_assignee_outbound` without `assignment_source` (and without `**kwargs`), this new kwarg will raise `TypeError` at runtime and break outbound assignee sync. The added tests mock the method and therefore wouldn’t catch a signature mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default evaluated once at module import, so every `AssignmentSource.from_integration(...)` instance carries the server-process start time instead of the enqueue time; any dedup/latency logic keyed on `queued` reports process uptime instead of sync delay, and the test only asserts `queued is not None` so it cannot catch this

[BUG] `assignment_source.to_dict()` returns a `datetime` in the dict passed to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`, causing `EncodeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` with the standard JSON serializer, so any assignment with a source never enqueues its outbound task, silently disabling cross-system propagation on the inbound path

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict(self)` (new file `assignment_source.py`), which will include the `queued` field as a raw `datetime`. That dict is then passed through Celery as task kwargs via `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(..., kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` in `integrations/utils/sync.py`. A raw `datetime` in Celery task kwargs will fail under JSON serialization (not JSON-serializable), so enqueuing can break when `assignment_source` is provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `sync_status_outbound` / `sync_status_inbound` got a new `assignment_source` parameter in the abstract signature but no caller anywhere passes one, making it dead surface with no implementation or test coverage; a resolve-triggered status ping-pong between two linked systems is not prevented, which is the sync-cycle class of bug this PR claims to fix

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an optional `assignment_source` parameter to the abstract `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound(...)` signature (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py) but the only concrete propagation of `AssignmentSource` shown in this PR is for assignee sync (GroupAssignee -> sync_group_assignee_outbound -> task -> installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source) and then `sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`). There is no corresponding change in this diff that passes `assignment_source` into any status-sync path, nor any tests covering status-cycle prevention. However, the finding’s claim that `sync_status_inbound` also got a new parameter is not supported by the shown diff (only `sync_status_outbound` changed here), and the assertion about “no caller anywhere” can’t be proven from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `from_dict` returns `None` on any parse failure and the task treats `None` as 'no source', which passes `should_sync` unconditionally, so a malformed/partially-serialized payload silently disables cycle prevention and re-opens the infinite sync loop; the failure should be loud (log + drop the sync) rather than a silent fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` returning `None` on `TypeError/ValueError` with no logging, and `sync_assignee_outbound` treating a parse failure the same as “no source” (`parsed_assignment_source = ... else None`) and then calling `installation.should_sync(..., parsed_assignment_source)`. In `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`, the cycle-prevention guard only runs when `sync_source` is non-`None`, so a malformed `assignment_source_dict` would bypass the new integration-id cycle check. However, the finding overstates that this makes `should_sync` pass “unconditionally” (it still checks the org integration config), and the infinite-loop scenario isn’t directly verifiable from the diff alone; it’s primarily a robustness/observability gap relative to the intended cycle-prevention behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `from_dict` performs no type validation, so a string `integration_id` (e.g., from JSON) constructs a 'valid' `AssignmentSource` where the same-integration cycle check compares str to int, evaluates `False`, and bypasses cycle prevention

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` simply does `return cls(**input_dict)` and only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` (new file `assignment_source.py`), but `dataclass` construction does not enforce the annotated types.
